徐培勛

S1120023@tss-c.com.tw 
 股價評價基礎： 
AI、半導體帶動用電需求激增，士電已接獲客戶需求，重電 T4 廠產能將於
4Q27 量產 ，2H28 開始貢獻營收 ；2027~2028 進入表後儲能工程認列高峰 ，
預估 2026/2027/2028 稅後 淨利 YoY+29%/+33%/+15% ， 稅 後EPS 
8.10/10.80/12.46 元，給予強力買進評等，目標價 250 元(20x 2028 EPS)，
潛在漲幅 22%。

營運近況摘要： 
士電成立於 1955 年，為台灣老牌變壓器生產商，技術來自三菱重工的技轉，
1H26 產品組合：電力配電(變壓器、配電盤)72%、車輛零件 15%、自動化設
備(工具機)10%、其他 3%。內外銷比 65%：35%。客戶包含：Mitsubishi 
Electric/Mitsuba Electric/ Panasonic/ Hitachi ABB/ Siemens/泓德能源/起
而行/和泰車。目前三個廠區都在新竹：電裝廠、新豐廠及重電廠。

2026 年重電 T1+T2 廠產能利用率提升，T3 廠、表後儲能小幅貢獻 
預估 2026 年營收 415 億元(YoY+12%)，因變壓器需求殷切，重電 T1、T2
廠產能利用率提升至 90%，重電 T3 廠 2025/9 開始量產，Lead time 1~1.5
年，4Q26 開始認列營收，2027 年全面貢獻；且公司在手 500MW 表後儲能
(太陽能儲能)統包案也開始貢獻營收 ； 毛利率21%(YoY+0.2ppts)， 因產品組
合較同期相同； 業外則有 金融資產 公允價值、匯兌利益挹注，稅後淨利
YoY+29%，稅後 EPS 8.15 元。

2027~2028 年 T3、T4 廠產能提升，表後儲能進入認列高峰 
展望 2027~2028 年，重電內銷(佔重電 80%)：政府希望強韌電網計畫完工
期限從 2033 年提早至 2028 年，依 2027 年預算書依然維持 2033 年完工，
2026/2027/2028 資本支出 46/118/155 億元，維持成長態勢。重電外銷(佔
重電 20%)： 為了因應全球 AI、半導體等強勁用電需求，重電 T4 廠將於
2027/9 量產，預期2H28 開始貢獻營收，2029 年全面貢獻，T1+T2 年產能
10GVA(十億伏安)，T3 可貢獻產能 5GVA、T4 再貢獻 5GVA，T4 主要客戶
為日本、美國電力市場，並專注在 345KV 變壓器生產。國內表後儲能(太陽
能)：公司在手 500MW 表後儲能案，若假設 2026/2027/2028 完工比率
10%/40%/50%計算，預計貢獻 7.5/30/37.5 億元，

「上櫃公司」 兩組，由70 項指標(1.維護股東權益及平等對待股東 11 項，占 16%，2.強化董事會結構與運作 18 項，占 25%，3.提
升資訊透明度 7 項，占 10%，4.推動永續發展 34 項，占 49%)編製而成，各組依評鑑成績高低分別公布七級距之公司名單，台新
投顧係引用民國 114(2025)年度之評鑑結果資料。

聯電 (2303 TT)  Buy

中長期業績展望佳，建議 Buy。  
投資建議 ：展望 2026 年， AI 基礎設施的需求正帶動整體市場
復甦，並外溢至記憶體、網通與電源管理領域，然消費性電子
(如手機、 PC) 終端需求仍偏弱，且庫存天數有微幅上升的跡象。
儘管如此，聯電預期其 2026 年整體晶圓出貨量仍將成長，特別
是在 22/28 nm 與 8 吋的市占率持續提升。聯電預估 2026 年 AI
相關營收將近 3 億美元，並預期 3 年內突破 10 億美元大關。預
估聯電 2026 年稅後 EPS 7.72 元。公司在先進封裝 (interposer 或
矽電容等 )、矽光子及 Intel 合作的 12nm 陸續取得進展，為 2027
年後中長期成長奠定基礎。雖聯電 2Q26 獲利大多以投資收益
為主， 3Q26 股市成長動能相對弱，可能壓抑業外收益，但本業
獲利逐步回升，建議 Buy ，目標價 169 元。  
2Q26 稅後 EPS 3.36 元：聯電 2Q26 營收為 687.33 億元，
QoQ+12.61% ，整體出貨量約當  12 吋晶圓 112.90 萬片，
QoQ+10.58% 。 2Q26 產能利用率增加至  85% 。 ASP 穩定向上。
2Q26 產能利用率增至 85% ， ASP QoQ 小增。 2Q26 毛利率增加
3.28 個百分點至 32.48% 。業外認列  302.36 億元收益，包含利
息收益  2.18 億元、匯兌收益 0.03 億元，認列投資收益  300.45 
億元 (1Q26 則為  49.97 億元投資收益 )。聯電 2Q26 稅後 EPS 
3.36 元 。 若不計算投資收益 ，2Q26 稅後 EPS 0.97 元，QoQ+9.31% 。 
預估 3Q26 稅後 EPS 1.47 元：預期 3Q26 在電腦、通訊及消費
性領域的需求動能將保持穩定。出貨成長主要由電源管理  IC 、
感測器及微控制器（ MCU ）的強勁需求所推動。 8 吋晶圓產品
線正迎來強勁反彈，預期 3Q26 產能利用率將有顯著改善；而  
12 吋產能目前已處於健康的利用率水位，足以支撐核心業務發
展。預 估 聯 電3Q26 晶圓出貨量 QoQ+7~9% ， 產能利用率約 90%。
ASP in USD QoQ+0% ，不過 2026 年的定價環境更具優勢。這主
要源於市場供需關係的結構性改善，毛利率增至約 35% 左右。
預估聯電 3Q26 稅後 EPS 1.47 元。

2 群益投顧 
  聯電 ESG ：  
聯電在 ESG 方面持續展現積極作為，並獲國內外多項評鑑肯定：  
永續策略與治理： ESG 由董事會與二位共同總經理組成的指導委員會全盤
規劃，持續以 「以人為本、與環境共生、與社會共榮」 為願景推動永續。 ESG
績效結合員工分紅與限制型股票條件，提升全員參與動能與企業凝聚力。  
環境面（ E）  
2025 年獲國際永續評鑑（如 FTSE Russell ）評為全台 ESG 表現頂尖企業，
半導體業唯一入選前 3。  
持續推動用水回收、能源效率提升，製程用水回收率在各廠均高於法規標
準。  
積極採購並投資離岸風電，與 CIP 渢妙風場簽 30 年綠電採購合約，展現對
2050 淨零承諾。  
社會面（ S）  
深化產學合作，與台灣 4 所大學半導體專班合作， 600 多位學生參與。  
啟動員工持股信託，落實多元薪酬政策，提升員工福祉並吸引人才。  
長期投入社會公益，如偏鄉關懷、青年培力、綠色創新等持續進行。  
公司治理（ G）  
董事會組成高度多元且獨立，獨董占三分之二、女性董事占三分之一。  
強化利害關係人溝通與資訊透明度，持續強化供應鏈 ESG 要求，並納入評
核與管理系統，推動價值鏈共榮。

預期近期股價將處於盤整  
建議降低持股

【投資評等調整機制】  
  投資評等係「首次」給予特定個股投資評等時，其前一日收盤價相較 3 個月
目標價之潛在上漲空間計算而得。個股投資評等分為四個等級，定義如上。
爾後的投資評等係依循「首次評等」，直到停止推薦。   
「強力買進」、「買進」及「區間操作」均有 upside 目標價。差別僅在於，
首次評等時潛在報酬率不同。「中立」則無目標價。  
一旦我們給予特定個股「強力買進」 、 「買進」或「區間操作」之投資評等，
就是責任的開始，爾後將透過各式研究報告作定期性、持續性追蹤基本面及
股價變化，直到停止推薦。  
停止推薦情境：  
1.  達目標價。  
2.  雖未達原訂目標價，但檢視基本面、訊息面、籌碼面等多方訊息，研
判股價上漲空間已然有限，將適時出具降評報告。  
3.  推薦後股價不漲反跌。

【免責聲明】  
  本研究報告僅提供予特定人之客戶作為參考資料「非經同意不得轉載」 。我
們並不確保此資訊的完整性與正確性，投資人應了解，報告中有關未來預測
之陳述可能不會實現，因而不應被依賴。而且此報告並非根據特定投資目的
或依預定對象之財務狀況所撰寫出來的，因此，此研究報告的目的，既非對
投資人於買賣證券、選擇權、期貨或其他證券相關之衍生性商品提供詢價服
務，亦非作為進行交易的要約。投資人應注意到相關證券之價值及收益，可
能會有無預警地上升或下降，產生投資回報金額可能比原始投資來得少的
情形。

 2H26 AI 動能續強

公司簡介 
華碩電腦成立於 1990 年，以生產個人電腦主機板起家，後來跨入筆記型電腦、無線
網通、及 3C 消費電子產品領域，以自有品牌「ASUS」銷售全球。2006 年以 ROG 
(Republic of Gamers) 品牌發展高階電競主機板及筆電等產品，樹立在電競市場的地
位，近年亦開始發展 AI 伺服器、AIoT 產品，搶攻 AI 商機。

➢ 2H26 AI 伺服器強勢成長  
華碩 8 月營收 949.6 億元 ，MoM+12.9%，YoY+51.2%， 公司預期3Q26 
PC 營收 QoQ+15%~20% ， YoY+20%~30% ， 零 組 件 營 收  
QoQ+5%~10%、YoY 持平，伺服器營收 QoQ+10%，YoY+150%。雖
然 PC 產業面臨缺料與關鍵零組件成本上升的挑戰，但記憶體的漲價帶
動 PC 售價上升，加上華碩高價值產品(如:高階電競、Copilot+PC 等)已
占營收 65%以上，此類產品的消費者價格敏感度較低，因此公司認為
3Q26 PC 業務價、量都優於 2Q26。 
華碩 AI 伺服器業務持續強勁 ， 客戶包含CSP、Neo cloud 以及主權 AI，
公司的伺服器營收當中，90%由 AI 貢獻(AI 中 HGX 約占營收 65%、
GB300 約占營收 35%)，預期伺服器 2026 全年營收 YoY+150%。投研
部估計華碩 3Q26 營收 2,773.6 億元，QoQ+7.6%，YoY+38.5%，毛利
率 16.3%，EPS 25.10 元。  
➢ IFA 2026 展出搭載 NVIDIA RTX Spark 的 ProArt PC 
華碩於 IFA 2026 展前發表會中 ， 已發表搭載 RTX Spark 的 ProArt P16、
ProArt P14、ProArt GR1X mini PC：1) ProArt P16 機身厚度 12.9 mm、
重量 1.77kg， 相較前一代薄14%、輕 9%， 為該系列歷來為最輕薄的16
吋版本；2) ProArt P14 機身厚度 13.9 mm、重量 1.48kg，搭載 90Wh
電池提供全天候續航；3) ProArt GR1X 尺寸 150×150×51 mm ，主打
機身僅掌心大小 ，同時兼具強大AI 運算效能 。 華碩表示，ProArt P16 與
ProArt P14 首波已預購一空，新品將於 4Q26 出貨。關於 AI PC 市場，
華碩之 AI PC 2Q26 已在消費型 NB 營收中達到 30%占比，公司認為未
來 2~3 年 AI PC、Edge AI 將引發產品升級循環 ， 對2H26 亦樂觀看待 。 
➢ 建議買進，目標價 1,130 元 
華碩 2H26 在 AI 伺服器與 AI PC 的帶動下展望樂觀，預期 2027 年 AI
伺服器能為公司帶來穩定的成長動能 。 華碩歷史PE 區間為 9X~18X，考
量公司營運展望正向 ， 投研部認為有利帶動其PE 回升 ， 買進目標價1,130
元(2027F PE 13X)。

### Page 1

Greater China Technology Hardware
Asia Pacific
Industry View In-Line
On the latest earnings call, Broadcom's CEO noted that the company is building
substrate capacity in its Singapore factory with a partner. We believe he was
referring to AST, the JV Broadcom has been developing with Toppan (7911.T, Not
Covered) since March 2024 (news). This is Toppan's first overseas substrate plant,
with phase 1 of the two-phase fab targeted to start production by EoY 2026. We see

Broadcom securing FC-BGA substrate supply rather than bringing production in-
house, and therefore expect limited impact on the current supply positions of
Unimicron and NYPCB.
On BT substrate pricing, the price hikes since 2H25 have been driven by raw material
cost inflation, including T glass, gold and copper. We have expected T glass supply
constraints to peak in 2026 and gradually ease from 2027 as more suppliers are
qualified. Thus, it would not surprise us if raw-material-driven price hikes plateau

going forward. That said, our OW thesis on Unimicron and NYPCB centers on ABF
substrate tightness, so we see limited impact from BT price fluctuations on our
ratings for both stocks.
Morgan Stanley does and seeks to do business with
companies covered in Morgan Stanley Research. As a result,
investors should be aware that the firm may have a conflict of
interest that could affect the objectivity of Morgan Stanley
Research. Investors should consider Morgan Stanley

communications with a subject company, public appearances
and trading securities held by a research analyst account.
Key Takeaways
NYPCB's share price was down 12% in the past two trading days (vs. TAIEX up
0.8%).
Investors have asked us if NYPCB would face share losses if Broadcom (AVGO,
covered by Joe Moore) were to produce substrates on its own.
Separately, we have been receiving questions from investors about the pricing
outlook for BT substrate in 4Q.

We see limited impact on our OW thesis for Unimicron and NYPCB, both of which
produce BT substrates and are Broadcom's incumbent suppliers.

Valuation Methodology and Risks
Unimicron (3037.TW)
Base case, residual income (RI) valuation model, which we think derives the most accurate
value of the firm given that it takes into account cost of equity. We use a cost of equity of 9.2%
[risk-free rate of 1% (10-year Taiwan government note yield), equity risk premium of 8.7%, and
a beta of 1.0], a medium-term growth rate of 15%, and a terminal growth rate of 3%.
Risks to Upside
n Better-than-expected ABF substrate demand from PC and server customers

n Capex cuts; halt to its capacity expansion plan
n Continued yield issues of alternative technology that doesn't require substrate (e.g.,
CoWoP)
Risks to Downside
n Sudden demand shortfall
n Technological change that would not require ABF substrates
n Intensifying competition
n Yield issues or production hiccups when ramping new capacity
Nan Ya PCB (8046.TW)
Base case, residual income (RI) valuation model, which we think derives the most accurate

value of the firm given that it takes into account cost of equity. We use a cost of equity of 9.3%
[risk-free rate of 1% (10-year Taiwan government note yield), equity risk premium of 8.7%, and
a beta of 1.0], a medium-term growth rate of 17%, and a terminal growth rate of 3%.
Risks to Upside
n Better-than-expected ABF and BT demand
n Faster-than-expected pickup in AI and 5G demand
n Stronger-than-expected ASP hike
n Continued yield issues of alternative technology that doesn't require substrate (e.g.

CoWoP)
Risks to Downside
n Sudden demand shortfall, creating headwinds for ABF substrate demand and pricing
n Technological change that would not require ABF substrates
n Intensifying competition

WinWay Technology
Valuation
We value WinWay using a PE-based approach that factors in earnings momentum and likely expansion of its addressable
market. Our target price of NT$11,500 is derived from applying c.41x to 2H27E-1H28E EPS, higher than the upper end of its
long-term PE range, which we believe is justified given the company's entrenched position in the high-end AI GPU testing
supply chain, rising contribution from coaxial socket and SLT solutions, and the increasing value of test content per module.

With these structural drivers in place, and as we believe the market is starting to value it as an AI/HPC play (rather than a
consumer electronics stock), we expect the multiple to hold at a premium relative to its historical averages.
Risks
Our quant rating system rates the WinWay stock High Risk based on its historical volatility.
Key downside risks that could impede the stock from reaching our target price and our earnings forecasts include: 1) client and

sector concentration – specifically any delays in US AI GPU product roadmap could impact the business outlook for WinWay; 2)
intensifying competition in coaxial and hypersockets from global peers; 3) faster-than-expected testing algorithm
optimization, which could shorten testing durations and reduce the anticipated hardware demand multiplier; and 4) delay of
MEMS Phase 2 mass production.

Guide to Citi Research Fundamental Research Investment Ratings:
Citi Research stock recommendations include an investment rating and an optional risk rating to highlight high risk stocks.

Risk rating takes into account both price volatility and fundamental criteria. Stocks will either have no risk rating or a High risk
rating assigned.
Investment Ratings: Citi Research investment ratings are Buy, Neutral and Sell. Our ratings are a function of analyst
expectations of expected total return ("ETR") and risk. ETR is the sum of the forecast price appreciation (or depreciation) plus
the dividend yield for a stock within the next 12 months.  The target price is based on a 12 month time horizon. The Investment

rating definitions are: Buy (1) ETR of 15% or more or 25% or more for High risk stocks; and Sell (3) for negative ETR. Any covered
stock not assigned a Buy or a Sell is a Neutral (2). For stocks rated Neutral (2), if an analyst believes that there are insufficient
valuation drivers and/or investment catalysts to derive a positive or negative investment view, they may elect with the approval
of Citi Research management not to assign a target price and, thus, not derive an ETR. Citi Research may suspend its rating

and target price and assign “Rating Suspended” status for regulatory and/or internal policy reasons. Citi Research may also
suspend its rating and target price and assign "Under Review" status for other exceptional circumstances (e.g. lack of
information critical to the analyst's thesis, trading suspension) affecting the company and/or trading in the company's
securities. In both such situations, the rating and target price will show as “—“ and “-“ respectively in the rating history price

chart. Prior to 11 April 2022 Citi Research assigned “Under Review” status to both situations and prior to 11 Nov 2020 only in
exceptional circumstances. As soon as practically possible, the analyst will publish a note re-establishing a rating and
investment thesis. Investment ratings are determined by the ranges described above at the time of initiation of coverage, a
change in investment and/or risk rating, or a change in target price (subject to limited management discretion). At times, the

expected total returns may fall outside of these ranges because of market price movements and/or other short-term volatility
or trading patterns. Such interim deviations will be permitted but will become subject to review by Research Management.
Your decision to buy or sell a security should be based upon your personal investment objectives and should be made only
after evaluating the stock's expected performance and risk.

transceiver demand, and we expect both companies to gain more share with more CCL
capacity to be ready in 2027/28 (see here and here).

products, but also seeing a significant margin expansion opportunity from the high-end
AI PCB and ABF substrate products, where we also see a strong demand outlook (see our
AI PCB industry report here and our ABF substrate industry report here).

### Page 3

Investment Thesis & PT methodology and risks

Investment Thesis - Zhen Ding Technology 
Zhen Ding Technology (ZDT) is the global leading PCB supplier (top 1 in market share in 
sales) with 7-10% market share, and started its ABF substrate business from 2023 in 
Shenzhen, China; it has the highest ABF revenue exposure to the China market compared 
to all other ABF substrate suppliers. We believe ZDT will hold more than 40% ABF 
substrate market share in China by 2027E (up from 31% in 2024) and benefit the most 
from the strong and growing China ABF substrate market (53% 2025E-27E CAGR) due to 
the increasing in-sourcing ratio for the AI computing ASIC/GPU market in China. We also 
expect the increasing foldable smartphone penetration rate in the long term to drive 
ZDT’s FPC TAM, and account for 50% of the company’s total revenue in 2027E. We see 
further revenue upside potential from foldable phones. We are Buy rated mainly due to 
our positive view on the company’s China ABF substrate business opportunity, which 
should not only drive ZDT’s revenue growth, but also improve its OPM level in the long 
term. We see upside for the stock price considering the company’s solid growth 
opportunity, and our TP implied P/E multiple is still lower than the company’s past 10+ 
year P/E average, which we believe is fair considering the potential upside from China 
ABF substrate market and increasing foldable phone penetration rate.  
Valuation: Our 12-month TP of NT$925 is based on a SOTP valuation methodology, 
including (1) 3.5x blended 2028E P/B for ABF & BT substrate, (2) 20x 2028E P/E for 
high-growth AI server/switch related PCB (in line with industry average), and (3) 8x 
2028E P/E for low-growth consumer electronics PCB (in-line with industry downcycle 
average valuation).  
Key downside risks include: (1) weaker-than-expected iPhone demand or slower 
content upgrade, (2) delay in new substrate capacity or slower-than-expected yield rate 
ramp up progress, and (3) fiercer competition in China ABF market. 
Investment Thesis - Elite Material  
EMC, a key supplier of high-end HDI material (70%+ market share) and SLP material 
(90%+ market share), has been focusing on the high-speed switch/server CCL market for 
3-5+ years. We are positive on its market share trajectory in the server industry and 
expect EMC to increase its share from <10% in the Purley generation to 15-20%/20+% 
in the Whitley/Eagle Stream platforms. EMC is also proactively expanding its share in the 
switch market (40%/30%+ in 2024/23 vs. <5% before 2019), with an expanding AI 
customer base (only one 400G customer in 3Q20, to being one of the largest suppliers in 
2023), which should continue to benefit the company’s top/bottom line growth over

Investment Thesis - Taiwan Union Technology Corp.

TV panel prices to stay flat MoM in September: Mainstream 32", 43", 55", 65" and
75" TV panel prices are all expected to stay flat for the month of September. This is
consistent with our expectations. On the demand side, although overall demand is
lackluster, there is still some seasonal restocking demand from brand customers to
prepare for  year-end promotion campaigns. On the supply side, panel makers remain

disciplined on output control and plan some annual maintenance to adjust
utilization during the coming October holidays in China. On a quarterly average
basis, we expect TV panel prices to decline by low-single-digit % QoQ in 3Q26.
IT panel prices to stay flat MoM in  September: Monitor and notebook panel prices
are expected to stay flat MoM during the month. Both applications are  seeing
slower demand in  2H26 post the earlier restocking  in 1H26 amid concerns about

increasing component costs. That said, panel makers are under cost pressure and
reluctant to given more price concessions. On a quarterly average basis, we expect
IT panel prices to remain flat QoQ in 3Q26.
Risk/reward less attractive: We think the current valuation for Taiwanese panel
names AUO (2409.TW; 1.5x P/B) and Innolux (3481.TW; 1.7x P/B) have already baked
in some expectations of glass in advanced packaging starting to make revenue
contribution in 2028. Nonetheless, some supply chain players think this might take

longer, and there seem to be many suppliers from different supply chains vying for
this opportunity as well, which could be a potential risk to monitor. In China, we
prefer BOE (000725.SZ; 1.4x P/B) over TCL (000100.SZ; 1.7x P/B), on its scale
advantage and faster progress in glass core substrates.
Morgan Stanley does and seeks to do business with

and trading securities held by a research analyst account.
Key Takeaways
Seasonal restocking along with disciplined output control should help stabilize
TV panel prices in the coming months.
IT panel prices are expected to stay roughly flat in coming quarters as well.
Potential opportunities for glass in advanced packaging seem  already  priced in,
with the risk in commercialization timing and competition worth monitoring.

TV Panel Prices Trending Down in 3Q26
TV panel prices started to edge up at the beginning of this year, rising 1% MoM in January,
2% MoM in February and 2% MoM in March. April, May and June were largely flat, while
July was down 2% MoM and August was down 1% MoM, in line with our expectation that
TV panel prices would start trending down from 3Q26.  That said, we do not expect a
significant decline as supply-side discipline should provide downside support.

Below-Seasonal Panel Shipments in 2H26
Over the past decade, TV panel shipments have typically been split 49%:51% between 1H
and 2H. In 2026, we expect the mix to skew toward 1H, as TV brands restocked ahead of
major promotional events, including the Winter Olympics in February, the FIFA World Cup
in June-July, and China's 618 shopping festival. We see no clear evidence that these events

will materially boost global TV demand, but they have historically shifted shipment timing
across quarters. As a result, we expect the restocking momentum seen since the start of
the year to fade, with panel order momentum slowing in 2H26.
Display Fab Utilization To Be at ~85% in 3Q26
Stronger TV panel shipments supported display fab utilization of ~80% in 4Q24 and 82%
in 1Q25. Utilization declined to 78% in 2Q25 as brands adopted a more cautious stance

following earlier pull-ins and as the impact of China's trade-in program moderated.
Utilization rebounded to 80-85% in 3Q25 as brands restocked for year-end promotions
and remained at similar levels in 4Q25 despite seasonal softness as well as in 1Q26.
Industry utilization stayed broadly flat QoQ, at 80-85% in 2Q26, reflecting continued
supply discipline, while we expect a slight uptick in 3Q26.
Over the medium to long term, we continue to believe the display industry is undergoing

structural change. Chinese panel makers have shifted their focus from top-line growth to
profitability, while lower government subsidies have reinforced supply discipline. We
believe investors increasingly recognize that the industry's production-to-order model can
remain sustainable, particularly as panel price cycles shortened to quarters in 2023-24 vs.
multiyear cycles in the previous decade. Consolidation actions, including LG Display's sale
of its Gen 8.5 Guangzhou fab to TCL and Sharp's closure of its Gen 10 Sakai fab, also

support a healthier supply backdrop (for more information, see Display – Structural

Morgan Stanley Research 5
Risk/Reward Fair After Recent Correction
We view risk-reward as broadly balanced following the recent correction in panel stocks.
Below are our current views:
• AUO (2409.TW, Derrick Yang): We rate AUO Equal-weight with a PT of NT
$27.00, based on a 1.4x 2026e P/B multiple. While we believe the current round of
TV panel price increases is nearing an end, major panel makers should continue to
demonstrate solid supply discipline, providing downside support. We appreciate

AUO's efforts to diversify its business, but meaningful earnings contributions are
likely to take time.
• BOE (000725.SZ, Derrick Yang): We prefer BOE due to its scale advantage,
higher exposure to display, and faster progress in glass core substrates. Our PT of
Rmb9.30 is based on 2.5x 2026e P/B, which we view as reasonable given our
estimated ROE of 5-8% over 2026-28 compared with BOE's average P/B of 1.1x and
ROE of 2-4% during 2023-25.
• Innolux (3481.TW, Derrick Yang): In semiconductors, our supply chain checks

suggest that Innolux is participating in a foundry customer's glass core substrate
project. However, we do not expect meaningful contributions before 2028, and
additional competitors could enter as the industry moves toward mass production.
We maintain our Equal-weight rating and PT of NT$60.00, based on a 2.1x 2026e
P/B multiple.
• LG Display (034220.KS, Ryan Kim): Meaningful OLED revenue contribution
should increasingly improve earnings from 2H25, but potentially weaker end-

markets keep us from turning bullish on LGD. The stock trades at 0.7x 2026e P/B
vs. a historical mid-cycle level of 0.5x.
• TCL (000100.SZ, Derrick Yang): We are EW with a price target of Rmb4.70 (1.7x
2026e P/B). The stock is trading at 1.7x 2026e P/B vs. its mid-cycle average of 1.4x
since 2022.
• Greater China DDIC supply chain implications – Novatek (3034.TW, Daniel Yen):
Our Underweight thesis reflects weaker PC, smartphone and automotive demand,

gross margin pressure, and a lack of new growth drivers. That said, Novatek's
OLED DDI roadmap appears more competitive than those of its key Korean peers
in terms of both performance and cost, helping it gain share in Apple's iPhone
supply chain.

Morgan Stanley Research 7
Where We Could Be Wrong
• Stronger end-demand: If end-demand for major applications turns out to be
better than expected, there could be stronger panel shipments and less panel price
pressure.
• More stringent output control: If major panel makers collectively adjust
utilization to an extreme extent, they could mitigate pricing pressure in the case of
softer demand.
• Non-commodity display business: If the non-commodity business progresses

faster than expected, panel makers could show better financial results.

Aspeed Technology (5274.TWO)
09 September 2026 Citi Research

Aspeed Technology
Company description
Established in 2004 and listed in 2013, Aspeed is a leading IC design
company based in Taiwan focusing on baseboard management controller
(BMC) solutions. Aspeed started the business by targeting datacenter
servers/white-box markets and has been working closely with server ODMs.
Following the acquisition of Emulex Pilot from AVGO/Broadcom in 2016,

Aspeed successfully expanded its product lines, IP pool as well as customer
base and became the largest BMC supplier with c.70% of global market share.
Other than BMC, Aspeed is also broadening its product portfolio by including
bridge IC (BIC; or mini-BMC), platform firmware resilience (PFR) solutions and
input/output (I/O) expander, aiming to maximize the dollar content it could
generate per server motherboard.
Investment strategy
We rate Aspeed shares a Buy. As a leading BMC supplier with c.70%+ global

market share, it has been riding the strong momentum underpinned by a
recovery of general-purpose servers and upticks in AI servers. We expect the
growth to continue. Apart from being in a dominant position for the supply of
upcoming GB200 server BMCs with higher dollar content and better capex
efficiency, new product launches including AST2700, PFR, I/O expander and
Cupola 360, as well as steady growth in general-purpose servers should also
act as key drivers for the company.

Valuation
We value Aspeed at NT$25,000 based on a historical mid-cycle multiple
(since 2020) of 50x 2028E EPS, as we believe it fairly reflects the company’s
earnings performance and industry dynamics, secular growth trends, and
Aspeed’s strong supply chain position, as well as robust earnings growth
amid margin expansions.
Risks
Our quant rating system rates the Aspeed stock High Risk based on its
volatility over the past year, which we think is unwarranted given the

company's dominance and outlook in the BMC sector. Key downside risks to
our earnings forecasts and target price include: 1) weaker-than-expected
growth in servers; 2) slower-than-expected CPU platform migration; 3) peer
competition; and 4) limited progress in product diversification.

Guide to Citi Research Fundamental Research Investment Ratings:
Citi Research stock recommendations include an investment rating and an optional risk rating to highlight high risk stocks.

Risk rating takes into account both price volatility and fundamental criteria. Stocks will either have no risk rating or a High risk
rating assigned.
Investment Ratings: Citi Research investment ratings are Buy, Neutral and Sell. Our ratings are a function of analyst
expectations of expected total return ("ETR") and risk. ETR is the sum of the forecast price appreciation (or depreciation) plus
the dividend yield for a stock within the next 12 months.  The target price is based on a 12 month time horizon. The Investment

rating definitions are: Buy (1) ETR of 15% or more or 25% or more for High risk stocks; and Sell (3) for negative ETR. Any covered
stock not assigned a Buy or a Sell is a Neutral (2). For stocks rated Neutral (2), if an analyst believes that there are insufficient
valuation drivers and/or investment catalysts to derive a positive or negative investment view, they may elect with the approval
of Citi Research management not to assign a target price and, thus, not derive an ETR. Citi Research may suspend its rating

and target price and assign “Rating Suspended” status for regulatory and/or internal policy reasons. Citi Research may also
suspend its rating and target price and assign "Under Review" status for other exceptional circumstances (e.g. lack of
information critical to the analyst's thesis, trading suspension) affecting the company and/or trading in the company's
securities. In both such situations, the rating and target price will show as “—“ and “-“ respectively in the rating history price

chart. Prior to 11 April 2022 Citi Research assigned “Under Review” status to both situations and prior to 11 Nov 2020 only in
exceptional circumstances. As soon as practically possible, the analyst will publish a note re-establishing a rating and
investment thesis. Investment ratings are determined by the ranges described above at the time of initiation of coverage, a
change in investment and/or risk rating, or a change in target price (subject to limited management discretion). At times, the

expected total returns may fall outside of these ranges because of market price movements and/or other short-term volatility
or trading patterns. Such interim deviations will be permitted but will become subject to review by Research Management.
Your decision to buy or sell a security should be based upon your personal investment objectives and should be made only
after evaluating the stock's expected performance and risk.

Catalyst Watch and STV Upside/Downside calls: Citi Research may also include a Catalyst Watch or STV Upside or Downside
call to indicate the analyst expects the share price to rise (fall) in absolute terms over a specified period of 30 or 90 days in
reaction to one or more specific near-term catalysts or events impacting the company or the market. A Catalyst Watch will be
published when Analyst confidence is high that an impact to share price will occur; it will be a STV when confidence level is

moderate. A Catalyst Watch or STV Upside/Downside call will automatically expire at the end of the specified 30/90 day
period. The Catalyst Watch will also be automatically removed if share price performance (calculated at market close) exceeds
15% against the direction of the call (unless over-ridden by the analyst). The analyst may also remove a Catalyst Watch or STV
call prior to the end of the specified period in a published research note. A Catalyst Watch/STV Upside or Downside call may be

our ratings distribution table for our Catalyst Watch/STV Upside/Downside rating system. However, we reiterate that we do
not consider No View to be a recommendation. For all Catalyst Watch/STV Upside/Downside calls, risk exists that the
catalyst(s) and associated share-price movement will not materialize as expected.

Summary: Driven by strong AI/HPC demand, all three companies set new revenue 
milestones: Winway (TWD 1.71bn, +6.6% MoM, +233.4% YoY), MPI (TWD 2.05bn, 
+13.4% MoM, +69.9% YoY), and CHPT (TWD 638m, +3.9% MoM, +54.3% YoY). With 
Winway’s capacity expansions tracking ahead of schedule, MPI set to begin shipping CPO 
insertion 3 products in 4Q26 alongside ASP hikes in late-3Q26, and CHPT nearing a 
qualification for its turnkey CPU ASIC project, the sector offers resilient sequential growth 
visibility through 2H26 and potential earnings upside heading into 2027.

What’s new: Following the conclusion of SEMICON Taiwan, we have observed a marked 
uptick in investor enquiries regarding the semiconductor test interface supply chain. As 
AI/HPC architectural transitions, and the increasing complexity of 2.5D/3D packaging drive 
structural content gains, investors have focused increasingly on capacity visibility and 
technological roadmaps across the socket and probe card segments. In the note, we recap 
the latest August monthly revenue figures and synthesize key market dynamics across our 
coverage universe.

WinWay Technology (6515 TT, TWD7,280, Buy [1]) 
• Aug revenue result: Monthly revenue reached TWD 1.71bn ( +6.6% MoM, +233.4% 
YoY), bringing 1-8M26 cumulative revenue to TWD 9.81bn (+97.9% YoY). Jul-Aug sales 
reached 72% of our 3Q26E revenue, tracking ahead of our expectations.

• Product mix & catalysts: Growth remains anchored by aggressive tape-outs from 
North American GPU leaders and cloud hyperscalers. Shipments of proprietary coaxial 
test sockets and advanced wafer-level vertical probe cards expanded sharply. While the 
market may expect meaningful revenue contributions from CPO sockets or probe cards, 
we believe it will account for mid-single digit in 2027E and high-single digit in 2028E.

• Outlook: The company maintained a constructive stance on order visibility and 
persistent demand-supply tightness. Management reaffirmed that 2Q26 marked the 
near-term cyclical trough, guiding for sequential revenue expansion on a QoQ basis 
moving forward. Our supply chain checks indicate that capacity expansion execution is 
tracking ahead of schedule compared with last month. With Winway poised to bring 
additional capacity online in 2027, we suggest investors monitor the company’s 2H26 
earnings call (mid-Nov) for further clarity on its 2027 capex and capacity roadmap.

• Valuation: We have a Buy (1) rating with a 12-month TP of TWD10,000, based on a 
target PER of 70x applied to our 4-quarter-forward EPS forecast. Based on our 
2027/28E EPS, the stock is currently trading at PERs of 36.9x/19.5x, vs. its previous 
highs of 80-90x. Downside risks: heavy reliance on major US AI chipmakers and; 2) 
intensifying competition that could erode design wins.

MPI Corporation (6223 TT, TWD5,615, Buy[1]) 
• Aug revenue result: Monthly revenue surpassed the TWD 2bn milestone for the first 
time, reaching TWD 2.05bn (+13.4% MoM, +69.9% YoY), bringing 1-8M26 cumulative 
revenue above TWD 13.0bn. Jul-Aug sales reached 63% of our 3Q26E revenue 
estimate, tracking slightly below our expectations.

Chunghwa Precision Test Tech (CHPT, 6510 TT, TWD3,610, Buy [1])

forward, steady deliveries of AI GPU test boards, alongside the forthcoming volume 
ramp of custom AI ASICs, should underpin sequential revenue growth.

• Outlook: Our supply chain checks indicate CHPT is competing for three AI/HPC probe 
card turnkey programs, comprising a CPU ASIC, an AI ASIC program for a US 
automotive client, and another AI ASIC program for Taiwanese clients. The automaker

probe cards for validation in November, with validation results expected by end-2026.

successful qualification would provide incremental top-line upside into late-2026, while 
serving as a significant catalyst for 2027 revenue upgrades and valuation expansion.

2027/28E EPS, the stock is currently trading at PERs of 30.2x/24.0x, vs. its peak of 68x. 
Downside risks: 1) project delays and utilisation risk; and 2) loss of market share.

EQUITY: TECHNOLOGY
SDI Corporation   2351.TW 2351 TT
Global Markets Research
11 September 2026
Stronger power lead frame outlook in 2H26-2027F
Heat spreader products the cherry on top; maintain Buy
We see further 2026/27F growth potential from power lead frame and heat spreader
Our recent industry channel checks suggests: 1) stronger power lead frame demand, 
especially from AI datacenter related in 2H26-2027F: As mentioned in our previous note, 
global integrated device manufacturers’ (IDM) 3Q26E sales outlook continues to show strength 
(3Q26E weighted average revenue y-y of +17% / q-q of +7%, vs +18% / +11% in 2Q26; this 
implies the fifth quarter of y-y expansion since 3Q25). Specifically, a few of SDI’s key IDM 
customers at their 2Q26 earnings calls raised 2026-27E AI datacenter revenue with stronger 
demand and faster capacity expansion (two customers’ 2027E-related sales should double y-y, 
according to our channel checks). We expect SDI’s 2027F power lead frame revenue from AI-
related field to realize 134% y-y growth (15% of total sales vs 8% in 2026F), with 60 ongoing 
projects currently; and 2) favorable pricing and product mix leading to better 2026/27F 
margin profile: Given supply tightness across several end markets, we expect further pricing 
improvement for SDI in 2H26F, after two rounds of price hikes in 1H26. In addition, given 
stronger demand from auto and AI datacenter (with GM better than other end markets), we 
expect SDI’s 2H26F/FY27F GM to reach 22.1%/23.0% vs 20.0% in 1H26.
2026-27F to mark the milestone of heat spreader business development
In addition to continued capacity expansion for power lead frame products, SDI’s management has 
decided to add more stamping equipment (ranging from 100-ton, 200-ton, to500-ton) in 2026-27E 
to handle increasing demand for its newly-developed product – heat spreader (including hat, cavity, 
ring/stiffener, and micro-channel lid, or MCL). The company will focus on automotive, ASIC/CPU, 
and networking in AI datacenter fields. Given superior manufacturing capability (20-30µ coplanarity 
vs 50-70µ of industrial average), it has secured four major orders from OSAT, auto, and IC design 
customers, with management expecting major revenue contribution from 2027E (we estimate 
3%/7% of 2027/28F total sales). We believe there can be sales and earnings contribution upside 
once we are able to confirm more order receiving from higher-end products.  
Raise 2026/27F EPS assumptions by 8%/17%; TP raised to TWD327
We raise 2026/27F sales and earnings growth (Fig. 1) with stronger order placing from global 
IDM customers, along with initial revenue contribution from heat spreader products. Our new TP 
of TWD327 is based on an unchanged multiple of 28x 2027F EPS of TWD11.68 (previously 28x 
2H26-1H27F EPS of TWD8.96), vs SDI’s historical average of 22.5x since 2015 (a range of 5.6x 
to 70.6x). The stock currently trades at 20x/16x 2027/28F EPS.

Company profile
SDI is a leading global semiconductor lead frame supplier headquartered in Taiwan. The company is the largest power semiconductor lead frame
manufacturer in the world, with its primary focus on automotive, industrial and AI applications.
Valuation Methodology
Our target price of TWD327 is based on 28x 2027F EPS of TWD11.68 vs historical average of 22.5x since 2015 with a range of 5.6x to 70.6x. The
benchmark for is this stock is TAIEX.

Risks that may impede the achievement of the target price
Downside risks: 1) slower-than-expected auto, industrial, and consumer electronic demand recovery, 2) delays of new products' mass production, 3)
pricing competition from global peers, and 4) dramatic copper price drop in short periods, which should be a negative impact on SDI's near-term GM.

Definition of Nomura Group's equity research rating system and sectors
The rating system is a relative system, indicating expected performance against a specific benchmark identified for each individual stock, 
subject to limited management discretion. An analyst’s target price is an assessment of the current intrinsic fair value of the stock based on an 
appropriate valuation methodology determined by the analyst. Valuation methodologies include, but are not limited to, discounted cash flow 
analysis, expected return on equity and multiple analysis. Analysts may also indicate expected absolute upside/downside relative to the stated 
target price, defined as (target price - current price)/current price.

SECTORS
A 'Bullish' stance, indicates that the analyst expects the sector to outperform the Benchmark during the next 12 months. A 'Neutral' stance, 
indicates that the analyst expects the sector to perform in line with the Benchmark during the next 12 months. A 'Bearish' stance, indicates that 
the analyst expects the sector to underperform the Benchmark during the next 12 months. Sectors that are labelled as 'Not rated' or shown as 
'N/A' are not assigned ratings. Benchmarks are as follows: United States: S&P 500; Europe: Dow Jones STOXX 600; Global Emerging 
Markets (ex-Asia): MSCI Emerging Markets ex-Asia. Japan/Asia ex-Japan: Sector ratings are not assigned.

Target Price
A Target Price, if discussed, indicates the analyst’s forecast for the share price with a 12-month time horizon, reflecting in part the analyst's 
estimates for the company's earnings. The achievement of any target price may be impeded by general market and macroeconomic trends, and 
by other risks related to the company or the market, and may not occur if the company's earnings differ from estimates.

## Document 107: 260914_gs_optical-tour

Source PDF: all report pdf/260914_gs_optical-tour.pdf
Report source: line報告備份
Date: 2026-09-14
Pages: 9
Extraction status: ok

### Page 1

1. Optical module demand outlook: Companies we visited remain positive on 
optical module demand, driven by AI server racks ramp up, optical module adoption 
expansion (from scale out to scale up / across), and specification upgrade. On global 
market demand on 800G and 1.6T, demand could be at 130m to 200m; for the China 
market, overall demand could also grow at mid double digits to 50m+ units, with the 
majority 800G and 400G, and 1.6T emerging. Nevertheless, companies we visited 
with also mentioned that tight raw material supply (e.g. DSP , lasers, PCB) could 
continue to cap shipments in 2027. The positive tone echoes our positive view on 
global demand, on which we raised 800G and above optical module demand by 39% 
/ 36% in 2027E / 2028E to 144m / 171m (report link). Supply chain positive tone 
reflects further upside to our estimates. 
2. Optical module competition: Companies we visited see pricing competition 
remaining healthy, with 800G optical module pricing decline within single digits in 
2027, and 1.6T optical module price to sustain at US$700+. Managements highlight 
that optical module is not a pure assembly but with multiple SKUs and require 
suppliers’ strong R&D and timely development as compared to telecom, the product 
cycle could shorten to 1-2 years in datacom vs. 5 years in telecom. Supply chain 
management and mass production capability are also important to win orders, 
especially under the current tight supply situation and clients’ requirements of 
diversifying production sites under geopolitical tension. Innolight, as the global 
leader works with supply chain closely, including R&D collaboration, invests directly 
in their suppliers, and pre-payment and long-term agreements to secure a

### Page 2

sustainable supply through cycles.
3. Laser supply: Chinese suppliers are ramping up capacity and capability in 200G EML,
supporting the 1.6T optical module ramp up in 2027. Nevertheless, shipment also
depends on other raw material supply (e.g. DSP), and customers penetration.
Everbright‘s laser capacity prepared for 2027 is EML slightly higher than CW laser, and
within the EML majority is for 100G, with the remaining for 200G; Dongshan Precision

highlights their 200G EML is already in mass production, while volume is still small
currently given the tight supply of DSP; nevertheless, the company also secured 10m
supply of DSP in 2027, supporting their lasers and optical modules shipment ramp up.
VPEC, global leading InP epiwafer supplier, also sees improving InP substrate supply, with
steady export permission from China government, more customers bringing InP
substrate, and growing second to fourth suppliers outside of China. VPEC’s MOCVD is

also in expansion, from current 62 MOCVD to 69 MOCVD by 2Q27, and planning a new
production site in 2027.
4. CPO timeline: As a new technology, CPO will naturally take time and could face
challenges in the path of commercialization. For example, laser suppliers see thermal
challenges for 300mW / 400mW CW lasers in ELS (external laser source), and is working
on 100mW+ with PA for NPO first. Optical module suppliers also see strong 3.2T NPO
optical engine demand across China and overseas markets. Nevertheless, equipment

suppliers remain the earliest beneficiary in CPO, with the strong testing and coupling
demand reflecting in equipment suppliers’ revenues in mid 2026. For example,
Robotechnik 2Q26 revenues were up 172% QoQ, or 141% higher than our estimates. As
we highlighted in Sep (report link), we estimate CPO switch at 10k / 92k / 131k units in
2026E-28E.
5. AI spending sustainability: Management highlighted that AI is a revolution, and we
are at an early stage of infrastructure spending and application development. It will be a

long cycle for the coming 10 to 20 years, and some of their customers are planning
beyond 2030. The demand for the coming 2 to 5 years remains very strong and
management highlighted their industry enjoys short return on investment, which is
around 1 to 2 years. Management highlighted the AI spending is not only building more
AI data centers, but also includes technology migration, such as making power
consumption more efficient, making data transmission faster, etc., driving the supply

chain growth. Compared to the internet bubble in the 2000s, management sees much
more transparency between end-customers (demand) and supply chain (supply), as end
customers are involved more in supply chain product development and capacity
investment, reducing the information gap between demand and supply, and reducing
the chance of double booking. Management noted that currently every module they
produce is being deployed in data centers, reflecting real demand.

6. Photonics IC scaling up: AI drives data transmission speed and bandwidth
requirement, leading to strong demand on Photonics IC, requesting it to catch up
Electrical IC automated production and testing ecosystem in 1 to 2 years, while EIC /
semiconductors has been developed for decades. The strong demand brings
opportunities to tool suppliers, across coupling and testing, which are necessary tools to
accelerate PIC production. Robotechnik / FiconTEC describes the number of tools they

target to ship in the coming 1 year would be over 50% of what they’ve shipped in the
past 25 years, reflecting the strong demand and orders visibility.

### Page 3

7. Testing - CPO earliest beneficiary: As a new technology, CPO naturally takes time
and faces challenges in the path of commercialization; however, we identify testing
equipment suppliers as the earliest beneficiaries, considering the expensive final module
means multiple testing during the production process is necessary, given the earlier a
failure is found, the lower cost a failure is. As a result, companies we visited continue to
see Insertion 2 (double-sided wafer-level testing) as necessary, and Robotechnik /

FiconTEC launched the new generation in 3Q26, which fully complied with the global
leading foundry’s communication infrastructure.
8. Testing - shortening time with KGD (know good die) at early stage: To facilitate
photonics IC scaling up, not only are more tools needed but better tools, requiring
suppliers’ strong R&D and execution, delivering continuous specification upgrade.
Robotechnik / FiconTEC, as global leaders in PIC testing, aim to shorten the wafer-level

testing time by 50-60% next year, and target 4x faster die-level testing next year.
Enlitech (7728.TWO, Not Covered) offers NightJar, a hyperspectral image system,
revealing AWG (arrayed waveguide grating) optical loss pathways with absolute optical
power mapping, allowing customers to KGD at Insertion 1 (PIC wafer testing) or Insertion
0 (PIC wafer early defect screening), saving failure costs.
9. Coupling - automated production becoming necessary in high-speed connection:

AI drives optical module towards high speed and high density / bandwidth, driving
demand on automated production. GMT (4573.TWO, not covered) showcased dual FA
active alignment equipment for 1.6T optical module, which could do the coupling for
both Tx and Rx simultaneously, saving 50% of coupling time compared to traditional
equipment. FitTech (6706.TW, not covered) has showcased an optical engine assembly
system, featuring passive / active alignment and customized development of coupling

algorithms, which could be used in multiple products: high-speed optical modules, ELS,
OCS, NPO, CPO, SiPh and optical chiplets. ASMPT has showcased MEGA multi-chip
bonding solution for complex multi-chip and photonics packaging applications,
combining high-precision placement with adhesive dispensing, UV fixation and 3D
inspection in one platform.
10. FAU & Laser specification upgrade: With optical networking expanding from scale
out to scale up, FAU and laser specification is also migrating. FOCI‘s FAU in 2026 to be

mainly 40 channels (starting in 3Q26) for 3.2T, followed by 80 channels (within 2026) for
6.4T, and 100 channels under R&D, per management. The company’s FAU enjoys several
customers across fabless, foundry, laser suppliers, etc. FOCI Aug revenues accelerated to
+20% MoM (vs. +9% MoM in Jul), reflecting the ramp up of high-end FAU. VPEC‘s
optoelectronics revenues enjoy strong growth on the back of strong CW lasers demand
and InP substrate supply getting better. Its InP epiwafer for CW lasers is also migrating

from 70mW / 100mW (scale out) to above 100mW (scale up, NPO) and 300mW /
400mW (scale up, CPO), along with expansion from CW lasers to 100G / 200G EML,
supporting its growth ahead.

Price Target Risks and Methodology - Zhongji Innolight Co.
Valuation: Our 12-m TP for Innolight A-share of Rmb2,645 is based on 35.6x 2027E P/E,
and our 12-m TP for Innolight H-share of HK$3,267 is based on a H-A premium of 13%.
We derive our target P/E multiple from the networking peers’ trading P/E vs.
forward-year fundamentals (NI YoY and OPM). Compared to Innolight’s historical trading
range, the target multiple reflects our view of its leading market position in high-speed

connections and product-mix upgrade toward SiPh optical modules, driving GM
expansion. We are Buy rated.
Key downside risks: 1) slower-/worse-than-expected 800G+ optical modules demand;
2) slower/worse-than-expected new optical devices ramp pace; 3)
faster-than-expected market share normalizing in 800G+ optical modules; 4)
geopolitical risks; and 5) worsening component supply situation to constrain shipment
growth.
Price Target Risks and Methodology - VPEC

Valuation: We adopt a discounted P/E method and apply a 22.2x target P/E on VPEC’s
2029E EPS, discounting back to 2027E at a COE of 10.5% (beta 1.7x, risk free rate 1.6%
and market risk premium at 5.1%), to derive our 12m TP of NT$793. Our target P/E is
based on a 0.4x PEG&M ratio derived from the average level of peers in the photonics
supply chain.
Key risk: Slower-than-expected SiPh business ramp up; weaker-than-expected
microelectronics demand from smartphones clients; IDM offers EPI wafer in-house.

Price Target Risks and Methodology - RoboTechnik
Valuation: Our 12-month target price of Rmb796 is based on a 20.7x 2031E P/E,
discounted back to 2027E at a COE of 11.3%. Our target multiple is derived from the
correlation between consumer electronic peers’ PEG&M (2026E P/E to 2027E NI YoY and
OPM), with RoboTechnik’s 2032E net income at 2% YoY and 2032E OPM at 32%.
Key downside risks: Fiercer-than-expected market competition; lower-than-expected

optical connection end demand; worse-than-expected photovoltaic market downcycle.
Valuation: Our 12-month target price of NT$833 is based on a 15.4x 2030E P/E,
discounted back to 2027E at a COE of 12.6%. Our target multiple is derived from peers’
correlation between forward-year trading P/E and earnings growth.
Key downside risks: Fiercer-than-expected market competition, technology migration
trends in optical networking, and slower-than-expected capacity ramp-up.

Price target methodology and risks - ASMPT
Valuation methodology: We are Neutral rated on ASMPT with a 12-month target price
of HK$177, which is based on a 24.9x 2030E discounted P/E (discounted back to 2027E).
Our target P/E is derived from correlation between peers P/E to the sum of NI YoY and
OPM.
Key upside/downside risks: 1) customers’ faster-/slower-than-expected adoption of
Advanced Packaging tools; 2) stronger-/weaker-than-expected demand from

automotive customers; and 3) stronger-/weaker-than-expected demand for traditional
IC packaging and SMT equipment.

Co-Tech Development Corp.  | Asia Pacific
Southeast Asia expansion points
to longer-term capacity upside
What’s new? Co-Tech’s board approved the establishment of a subsidiary in
Southeast Asia.
Our view: We expect the facility to primarily produce RG-series (advanced RTF)
copper foil, mainly used in general servers, switches or LEO satellites. Volume
production could begin in 2H28, with monthly capacity exceeding 500 tons. We
currently model Co-Tech’s RG-series capacity at 1,000 tons by end-2026 and 1,200

tons by end-2027. The Southeast Asia expansion therefore implies upside to our
current capacity assumptions, assuming all else remains unchanged, with
contribution likely starting in 2H28. We also believe adding RG-series capacity in
Southeast Asia could free up existing Taiwan capacity for higher-end HVLP4+ copper
foil production. Stay OW.

First Read
Parade Technologies
2026 Taiwan Summit: Near-term outlook
impacted by softer NB demand
Q326 revenue tracking toward lower-end of guidance
Parade attended our 2026 Taiwan Summit on Sep 14th. August sales of NT$1,327 mn
was down 2% and flat YoY. QTD sales only reached 57% of UBSe and Street estimates,
and Parade now expects its Q326 sales could come in at the lower-end of its US$139–
153 mn guidance range, likely due to softer NB demand. Parade's GM declined by 0.1

pp QoQ to 40.2% in Q226 on OSAT price hike, as the Taiwanese OSATs have allocated
more capacity to AI-related products. Parade noted it has been adding new OSAT
partners in Korea, China, and Malaysia, while also adjusting its ASPs in Q326. It noted its
Q326F GM should come in within its 40-44% guidance range, but we believe the GM
expansion will be more moderate given the cost headwinds. Q326F OPEX guidance is
reiterated at US$33-36 mn with full year OPEX growth to be within 5% YoY, and

effective tax rate for 2026F is guided to remain slightly above 10%. It has not provided a
specific outlook for Q426 but acknowledge the challenging outlook for the laptop
market. This is consistent with our recent checks within the NB display supply chain.
ASIC for CPU chipset to tape out soon for H227 mass production
Parade highlighted its deep expertise in high-speed connectivity and proprietary IP,
which enables it to deliver customized ASIC-like solutions to its customers. While its

initial focus was  display applications, it is now expanding  into CPU chipset. It is on-track
to tape out two chipsets for its CPU  customer, targeting  different PCIe channel
configurations. Comparing with its peers solution on 28nm node, Parade believes its
product  developed on 12 nm node  offers superior power efficiency. Parade noted the
CPU chipsets are  on track for mass production by H227, although we believe ASMedia's
solution will start to ramp from mid-2027 and will split the market share with Parade.

Exploring additional growth drivers for 2027
Parade also highlighted its ongoing effort to diversify away from traditional NB display  IC
business with several initiatives expected to contribute growth from 2027F. It sees good
revenue opportunity for  integrated touch solutions (TED/TTED), especially after the
potential adoption of touch display by  its standard-plus customer. For ACC cables, it will
supply redriver  with switch function, which should be a new growth engine in 2027F as

it believes copper and optical will co-exist in the next several years. Its USB4 retimer also
has good market share at non-Intel platform and management expects the penetration
to exceed  50% in 2027 vs 40%+ in 2026. Parade also noted its automotive business
should see strong sales growth in 2027, although we estimate overall contribution for
this segment remains at low-single-digit  % of total revenue.
Valuation: Rate NEUTRAL with NT$610 PT
We have a NEUTRAL rating on Parade with NT$610 PT,  based on 14.5x forward PE.

Company Description
Founded in 2005, Parade is a mixed-signal IC fabless design house headquartered in San Jose,
CA, specialising in high-speed interface and display solutions used in PCs, servers, consumer
electronics and display panels. Parade's display solutions (55% of 2024 revenue) include

embedded display port timing controllers (eDP TCON), source drivers and touch controllers.
Parade's high-speed interface solutions (45% of 2025 revenue) include signal conditioners
for USB, PCIe, SATA, etc, as well as protocol converters and USB controllers.
Valuation Method and Risk Statement
Our price target for Parade is based on target PE multiple.
Fabless integrated circuit (IC) design houses face a variety of uncertainties, including rapidly

changing technology, end-market demand, competition, employee turnover and foundry
wafer costs. They are also vulnerable to legal disputes over IP rights.
For Parade, we believe key risks include: 1) Demand dynamics in PCs/notebooks, TVs, servers,
etc., as any pickup or slowdown in these end-markets would directly impact Parade's growth
and new product rollouts. 2) The length of the qualification cycle or pace of adoption by
clients could be a key upside/downside risk to our thesis. 3) Potential new entrants in Apple's

IT display timing controllers could be a downside risk to our growth estimates. 4) Fiercer price
competition by global and Asian peers may pose downside risk to our growth and GM
forecasts. 5) Foundry and assembly cost changes could present upside/downside risks to our
GM estimates.

Investing in structured investments involves significant risks. For a detailed discussion of the risks involved in investing in any particular structured investment, you must read

the relevant offering materials for that investment. Structured investments are unsecured obligations of a particular issuer with returns linked to the performance of an
underlying asset. Depending on the terms of the investment, investors could lose all or a substantial portion of their investment based on the performance of the underlying
asset. Investors could also lose their entire investment if the issuer becomes insolvent. UBS does not guarantee in any way the obligations or the financial condition of any

issuer or the accuracy of any financial information provided by any issuer. Structured investments are not traditional investments and investing in a structured investment is
not equivalent to investing directly in the underlying asset. Structured investments may have limited or no liquidity, and investors should be prepared to hold their investment
to maturity. The return of structured investments may be limited by a maximum gain, participation rate or other feature. Structured investments may include call features and,

if a structured investment is called early, investors would not earn any further return and may not be able to reinvest in similar investments with similar terms. Structured
investments include costs and fees which are generally embedded in the price of the investment. The tax treatment of a structured investment may be complex and may differ
from a direct investment in the underlying asset. UBS and its employees do not provide tax advice. Investors should consult their own tax advisor about their own tax situation

before investing in any securities.

China's advanced packaging industry remains a secular AI-driven

growth story. But, we see rising overcapacity risk and prefer
equipment vendors and market share gainers.
Advanced packaging is becoming increasingly critical to AI GPU performance,
particularly in China. As AI accelerators require greater compute density, memory
bandwidth, and system-level integration, advanced packaging provides a key
pathway to improve performance. This is particularly important for China, where
restrictions on access to leading-edge semiconductor  equipment constrain further

front-end process scaling, increasing the strategic value of packaging-led
performance improvements. We are therefore constructive on the structural growth
outlook for China advanced packaging.
However, we are more cautious than consensus on how this TAM growth
translates into OSAT earnings. We see a growing risk of moderate overcapacity, as
attractive industry growth and margins encourage incumbent OSATs and new
entrants to add 2.5D/3D capacity. Our bottom-up analysis suggests China’s 2.5D

capacity could rise from 120k wafers in 2025 to 436k in 2027, while effective
demand remains constrained  by advanced-node yields and HBM availability. We
estimate industry utilization at only ~63% in 2027, suggesting stronger competition
could weigh on pricing and limit margin upside even as industry revenue continues
to grow.
We therefore prefer advanced-packaging equipment vendors over broad-based
OSAT exposure.  The ongoing capacity race requires substantial upfront spending,

regardless of whether the resulting OSAT capacity ultimately generates attractive
returns. At the same time, the migration from conventional packaging toward
2.5D/3D raises process complexity and equipment intensity per unit of capacity,
providing an additional structural growth driver for equipment suppliers. Aggregate
OSAT capex is already accelerating, supporting our preference for capex
beneficiaries including  ASMPT and ACM Research among our covered names.

Within OSATs, we prefer share gainers: upgrade JCET to OW; initiate SJ Semi at
EW. We upgrade JCET to Overweight with a Rmb90.2 PT, as we expect the company
to emerge as a meaningful share gainer in domestic 2.5D packaging,  and continued
mix diversification toward computing and automotive. We initiate SJ Semi at Equal-
weight with a Rmb118.4 PT. While it remains China’s leading 2.5D packaging vendor,
we believe its premium valuation already discounts much of its technology

leadership and AI-driven growth, while increasing competition, customer
concentration and HBM availability create a more balanced risk-reward.

Investment Summary
China advanced packaging: Structural AI growth, but value capture should favor
equipment vendors and OSAT share gainers. China's advanced packaging industry
remains a secular AI-driven growth story, but we see a growing divergence between
industry TAM growth and earnings capture across the value chain. Advanced packaging is
becoming increasingly critical to AI accelerator performance by enabling higher compute

density, memory bandwidth and heterogeneous integration through technologies
including wafer-level processing, RDL, TSV, chiplets, 2.5D integration, 3DIC and hybrid
bonding. This is particularly important in China, where restrictions on access to leading-
edge front-end semiconductor equipment increase the strategic value of packaging-led
performance improvements.
Exhibit 8: AI chip value chain (China vs. US) - we focus on China advanced packaging in this report

Source: Morgan Stanley Research
We expect China’s advanced packaging TAM to reach approximately Rmb100bn by
2029, implying a roughly 13% CAGR over 2025-29, while the chiplet / 2.5D segment
should grow substantially faster, reaching Rmb17.7bn by 2029 at a 40% CAGR. However,
we are more cautious than consensus on how this growth translates into OSAT earnings.
China’s 2.5D annual capacity is expected to expand from around 120k wafers in 2025 to
436k wafers in 2027, while effective demand is constrained by advanced-node yields, HBM

availability and customer qualification. We therefore estimate industry utilization at only
around 63% in 2027, suggesting moderate overcapacity could pressure pricing and limit
margin upside even as industry revenue continues to grow.

Three key debates
1. Will China's advanced packaging industry face oversupply? — We see
moderate overcapacity risk, particularly in 2.5D.
The market remains constructive on supply-demand, given strong domestic AI compute
growth, but we think capacity additions could run ahead of effective demand. Attractive

industry growth and margins are drawing incumbent OSATs and new entrants into
2.5D/3D packaging, while actual packaging demand is constrained by the availability of
qualified accelerator dies and HBM. In addition, a shift from CoWoS-S-like to CoWoS-L-like
architectures could create a capacity-mix mismatch, with excess S-like capacity even if L-
like capacity remains tight. Longer term, greater adoption of 3D integration could also
reduce the amount of 2.5D package footprint required per accelerator die

2. Who captures more value — OSATs or equipment vendors? — We
prefer equipment vendors.
Our key distinction is that OSAT earnings depend on capacity being filled, while
equipment revenues depend primarily on capacity being built. If our moderate-
overcapacity thesis is correct, aggressive OSAT expansion could dilute utilization and
pricing while still creating a strong order environment for equipment suppliers. The
technology transition also structurally increases equipment intensity: 2.5D/3D requires

additional fine-pitch RDL, TSV, wafer-level processing, temporary bonding/debonding,
high-precision die placement, TCB/hybrid bonding and advanced inspection. We therefore
expect equipment value per unit of packaging capacity to rise as China migrates toward
more complex architectures.
3. How much upside should investors assign to 3DIC, HBM packaging
and CPO? — Strategically important, but near-term earnings
contribution is likely overstated.
We view the current earnings opportunity as still primarily driven by 2.5D / CoWoS-like

capacity expansion, while 3DIC, HBM and CPO remain mainly medium- to long-term

### Page 6

M
Asia Pacific Insight
6
optionality. 3DIC could be particularly important in China as a workaround for constrained
front-end scaling, but high cost and compound-yield sensitivity remain key barriers.  We
estimate China’s 3DIC market may remain only in the tens of millions of US dollars over
the next 2-3 years. HBM is a large volume opportunity, but packaging value is still largely
retained within the memory ecosystem, limiting near-term independent OSAT value

capture. CPO has attractive long-term potential, but large-scale deployment is more likely
in 2027-28, implying limited contribution to China OSAT earnings over the next 1-2 years
Stock implications: Favor capex beneficiaries and share
gainers
We therefore see two preferred ways to gain exposure to China
advanced packaging.
First, equipment vendors offer the cleaner exposure to the capacity build-out. ACM
Research is a direct beneficiary through electrochemical plating, cleaning and other wet

processes, with advanced-packaging revenue already accelerating and panel-level
packaging moving closer to volume production. ASMPT is well positioned through TCB,
high-precision flip-chip and hybrid bonding, wherein increasing package size, finer
interconnect pitch and 3D integration should drive unit demand and mix toward higher-
value platforms.
Second, within OSATs, we prefer share gainers rather than broad industry exposure.
JCET is our preferred domestic OSAT as it is building 2.5D capacity from a low base,

improving customer visibility and expanding into computing, automotive, CPO and next-
generation packaging. We expect this to support structural share gains over the medium
term. By contrast, SJ Semi remains the domestic technology leader, with roughly 77%
share of China’s 2.5D market in 2025 and a clear lead in 3DIC commercialization, but we
believe its premium valuation already discounts much of this leadership. Competitive
capacity additions could also reduce its built-capacity share materially by 2027, while

customer concentration remains high.

Asia Pacific Insight

Debate 1: Will China's advanced packaging market face
oversupply?
Market view: Unlikely. China remains at the early stage of advanced packaging
adoption, while underlying demand is expected to grow rapidly, led by strong
domestic AI compute requirements. Looking ahead, structural growth in AI, data
centers, cloud computing, autonomous driving and high-end consumer electronics
should drive increasing adoption of advanced packaging. Against this backdrop, the

market expects demand growth to outpace capacity additions, supporting healthy
utilization and favorable industry economics for domestic OSATs.
Our view: Risk of moderate overcapacity. Firstly, more players, intensifying
competition,  and an attractive growth outlook is drawing more OSATs to enter the
market, which could drive capacity ramp-up ahead of demand increase. Secondly,
effective demand may be constrained by upstream bottlenecks, including yields at

advanced process nodes and the availability of HBM and related components.
Thirdly, as domestic accelerator chips migrate toward 3D integration, multiple
accelerator dies could be vertically stacked before being packaged alongside HBM.
This could reduce the amount of 2.5D packaging required per accelerator die
shipped assuming similar die sizes, as more accelerator dies can be integrated
within a given 2.5D package.
Where we could be wrong: 1) Domestic AI compute demand scales faster than

expected; 2) faster expansion of domestic advanced-node capacity and improved
domestic HBM availability; 3) the transition toward 3D integration is slower than
expected, resulting in a smaller reduction in 2.5D packaging demand.
Key metrics to monitor: 1) Domestic advanced packaging capacity; 2) domestic
advanced node capacity and HBM availability; 3) progress of domestic logic-die 3D
stacking technology.
We see a growing risk of moderate overcapacity, particularly in 2.5D packaging. While

we remain constructive on the structural growth of China’s advanced packaging market,
we think the market may be underestimating the pace of domestic capacity additions
relative to effective demand. Importantly, we distinguish between strong long-term TAM
growth and the near-/medium-term supply-demand balance. A rapidly growing industry
can still experience periods of excess capacity if supply is built ahead of customer
qualification, upstream component availability and actual accelerator shipments. We see

three reasons why this risk could become more visible over the next few years.
First, attractive growth prospects are encouraging increasingly aggressive capacity
expansion. Advanced packaging enjoys high gross margin and it has become a strategic
focus for incumbent OSATs and new entrants, with multiple domestic players (JCET,
Tongfu Micro, Huatian Technology, Forehope etc.) expanding 2.5D/3D-related capacity
simultaneously. Companies have an incentive to build ahead of confirmed demand, given

long equipment lead times and the strategic importance of securing domestic AI supply-
chain capacity. This creates a potential timing mismatch. Capacity can ramp relatively

### Page 9

Morgan Stanley Research 9
quickly once equipment is installed and qualified, while end-demand conversion depends
on customer product ramps and utilization.  Based on our bottom up analysis, we expect
China 2.5D packaging annual capacity to grow to 436k wafers in 2027, up from 120k
wafers in 2025, which is around 16% of non-China (TSMC mainly) capacity.

Second, on the demand side, upstream bottlenecks could constrain effective
packaging demand. The demand-side risk is that the end market demand for AI compute
may not translate directly into effective packaging demand. The immediate downstream
demand depends on the availability of qualified accelerator dies and HBM. Advanced-node
wafer yields are one potential constraint. Domestic AI accelerators increasingly require

sophisticated process technologies, and lower yields can reduce the number of known-
good dies available for packaging. We estimate AI GPU shipments by Chinese vendors will
reach 4.9mn units in 2027, up from 1.1mn units in 2025. Assuming around 21 chips per
wafer and overall yield of 85%, that indicates around 277k wafer demand in 2027.
HBM availability represents another major challenge. High-performance AI accelerators
increasingly depend on large amounts of high-bandwidth memory, and shortages in HBM

supply could effectively cap package output. In our CXMT initiation report, we estimated
3-4mn unit locally produced HBM units, but that could only support 0.75-1mn units of
GPU, with the rest still relying on foreign HBM supply. Other constraints, including on
substrates, advanced interconnect materials, thermal solutions and specialized equipment,
could have similar effects. In such a scenario, underlying AI demand could remain robust
while actual packaging utilization falls short of expectations. This distinction between end

demand and effective demand is central to our more cautious industry view.

Capacity mix is shifting from CoWoS-S-like to CoWoS-L-like solutions
Another important consideration is the mix of 2.5D packaging capacity being built in China.

Domestic advanced packaging players have generally started with CoWoS-S-like solutions
based on a full silicon interposer, while gradually developing more CoWoS-L-like
capabilities as AI packages become larger and more complex. This broadly mirrors the
technology evolution seen at TSMC, where CoWoS-S uses a silicon interposer, while
CoWoS-L combines an RDL-based interposer with local silicon interconnects to enable
greater package scalability and design flexibility. TSMC itself has shifted its development

focus toward CoWoS-L as HPC package sizes increase.
This transition could create a capacity-mix mismatch within China's advanced packaging
market. CoWoS-S-like capacity is currently more mature domestically and represents a
meaningful portion of existing and near-term capacity, whereas CoWoS-L-like capacity
remains at an earlier stage of ramp. At the same time, demand from newer generations of

### Page 11

M
Asia Pacific Insight
Morgan Stanley Research 11
high-performance AI accelerators is increasingly moving toward larger and more complex
packages, which should favor CoWoS-L-like architectures over time. Recent industry
indications suggest domestic CoWoS-L-like products are beginning to enter volume
production, while the broader industry is increasingly treating CoWoS-L as the next major
technology upgrade for 2.5D packaging.
As a result, we see greater overcapacity risk in CoWoS-S-like capacity than in CoWoS-L-

like capacity. S-like demand could begin to moderate as customers migrate toward L-like
solutions, potentially leaving some dedicated S-like capacity underutilized even as
aggregate advanced packaging demand continues to grow. This distinction is important
because headline 2.5D capacity numbers may overstate the supply that is actually suitable
for next-generation AI accelerators. A market can therefore simultaneously experience
excess S-like capacity and relatively tight L-like capacity.

Domestic players are partly mitigating this risk by building flexibility into portions of their
capacity. Where common process modules can support both S-like and L-like flows,
capacity initially used for S-like products can potentially be reconfigured toward L-like
production as customer demand migrates. This should reduce the risk that all S-like
capacity becomes structurally stranded. However, the conversion is unlikely to be
completely frictionless, given differences in interposer architecture, process flow,

equipment requirements and customer qualification. Therefore, nominally flexible capacity
should not necessarily be treated as immediately interchangeable between the two
technologies.
The implication for our overcapacity thesis is that the risk may increasingly be one of
capacity mix rather than aggregate capacity alone. In the near term, the faster build-out of
S-like capacity could result in declining utilization as demand begins to shift toward L-like

solutions. Over the medium term, continued growth in L-like demand and the gradual
conversion of flexible lines could absorb part of this excess. We would therefore monitor
S-like and L-like capacity, utilization and customer qualifications separately, rather than
relying solely on aggregate domestic CoWoS-like capacity when assessing the industry's
supply-demand balance.

Also, the transition from 2.5D toward 3D integration could change the relationship
between accelerator shipments and 2.5D packaging demand. Today, a typical high-end

accelerator architecture places compute die(s) and HBM side-by-side on an interposer or
equivalent 2.5D platform. As domestic accelerator vendors move toward more advanced
3D architectures, multiple accelerator dies could increasingly be vertically integrated
before being packaged alongside HBM. Assuming broadly similar die sizes, this could allow
more compute dies to be incorporated within a given 2.5D package footprint, meaning
2.5D packaging demand may grow more slowly than do accelerator die shipments. In other

words, rising AI accelerator volumes do not necessarily translate linearly into rising 2.5D
packaging units or area over the longer term.
Conclusion
We remain constructive on the structural growth outlook for China's advanced packaging
market, while seeing a risk of moderate overcapacity as capacity investment accelerates.
The market's bullish view is well supported by rapidly growing domestic AI compute
demand, continued semiconductor localization and the increasing importance of advanced

packaging in enabling higher system-level performance. Our concern is that effective
packaging demand may grow more slowly than AI demand due to component constraints,
while industry capacity could expand relatively quickly.
Packaging architecture adds another layer of uncertainty. If domestic AI accelerators
increasingly adopt 3D integration, vertically stacking multiple GPU dies could reduce the
amount of 2.5D package footprint required per GPU die, assuming broadly stable die sizes

and total die volumes.

Debate 2: Which vendors are the biggest beneficiaries of
China's advanced packaging business?
Market view: OSAT vendors. The market increasingly views advanced packaging
as a key technology enabler for domestic AI GPUs, particularly as China’s access to
advanced node semiconductor production equipment remains constrained. As
further transistor scaling becomes more challenging, advanced packaging provides

an alternative pathway to enhance system-level performance through chiplets,
higher integration density, and higher-bandwidth interconnects. Against this
backdrop, OSAT vendors could emerge as key beneficiaries of China’s AI compute
build-out.
Our view: Equipment vendors. As we discussed in Debate 1, we expect China's
advanced packaging to be in a moderate degree of overcapacity over the next few
years, so the  broad-based capacity build-out could intensify competition, pressure

pricing, and constrain gross margin upside. Equipment vendors, by contrast, are
better positioned to capture the current capacity expansion cycle. Regardless of
whether incremental OSAT capacity ultimately generates attractive returns, the
initial capacity build-out requires meaningful equipment investment.
Metrics to monitor: 1) Capex of OSAT vendors; 2) margin trend of OSAT vendors;
3) revenue and earnings  growth of OSAT vendors.
Where we could be wrong: 1) Stronger China AI compute demand  than our

expectation, outpacing the advanced packaging capacity addition,  leading to higher
gross margin for OSAT vendors; 2) technological breakthrough of OSAT vendors,
leading to cost saving and margin expansion.
Equipment vendors are better positioned than OSAT vendors to play
China's advanced packaging
In our report on  JCET: Slow recovery with share loss; downgrade to UW (Sep 24, 2024),
we had already argued that the biggest beneficiaries of China's advanced packaging would

be the equipment vendors, rather than the OSAT vendors. Our main argument was that
the advanced packaging opportunity for OSAT vendors comes at the expense of higher
R&D and capex, weighing on near-term earnings, while the equipment vendors are the
beneficiaries from the capex build-up.
What has changed since then is the volume ramp-up of China's AI GPU shipments, and the
rising demand for domestic 2.5D advanced packaging demand. As discussed in Debate 1,

we see moderate overcapacity as a result, which may intensify competition, pressure
pricing, and constrain gross margin upside for OSAT vendors.
Equipment vendors, by contrast, should benefit more directly from the capacity
expansion itself. Regardless of whether incremental OSAT capacity ultimately earns an
attractive return, building that capacity requires upfront investment in bonding,

### Page 14

lithography, deposition, plating, inspection/metrology, wafer handling and other back-end
equipment. In other words, OSAT earnings depend on capacity being filled, while
equipment revenues depend primarily on capacity being built. This distinction becomes
particularly important if our moderate-overcapacity thesis is correct. Aggressive OSAT
expansion could be dilutive to industry utilization and pricing while simultaneously

creating a strong order environment for equipment suppliers.
